answer: Interleaved Arrival Gate. Each new identity must complete its first ten transactions in a randomized order relative to peers, with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a per-epoch distribution; the gate rejects clusters whose timing variance is too low, since scripted sock-puppets arrive in tight, hollow bursts. An attacker must therefore simulate organic idle time across every fake agent, paying real wall-clock delay per identity plus jitter-tuning costs. Honest agents pass as a slow pearl forming; a sybil fleet spreads across slower island windows, multiplying its setup latency.
